paragraphs.source_en: Thus was decided the heir to the vast fortune and businesses of the Inugami clan, a man who, however, was fated to languish in a dark prison cell for several years.

paragraphs.source_en: Matsuko, who had been watching the scene before her with an air of satisfaction, took another pinch of shredded tobacco and filled her long-stemmed pipe. paragraphs.source_en: "Tamayo," said Matsuko as she quietly smoked her pipe.

paragraphs.source_en: "I have one more favor to ask of you."

paragraphs.source_en: Matsuko refilled her pipe with another pinch of tobacco from the drawer. "It's about Sayoko."

paragraphs.source_en: Startled at the mention of Sayoko's name, Takeko and Umeko looked at Matsuko's face, but the latter still sat calmly smoking her pipe, repeatedly emptying and refilling it with new pinches of tobacco. paragraphs.source_en: "No! No! No! It's the tobacco. The same poison that killed Wakabayashi. I didn't notice. I didn't notice. A doctor... somebody call a doctor!"

paragraphs.source_en: By the time the doctor had rushed to the scene, however, Matsuko Inugami---that most demonic woman, that extraordinary killer who had shocked the nation---lay dead, a trickle of blood seeping out from the corner of her mouth. It was a twilight so cold even the snow lay frozen over Lake Nasu.
